site_lede: Detailed notes for every topic in the Java full-stack roadmap — each concept with how it works, the rules, conventions, exceptions and edge cases, runnable examples, common mistakes and the interview angle.

topics.title: Git & GitHub
topics.lede: Version control from your very first commit to professional team workflows — how Git stores your work, the daily commands, GitHub and remotes, branches and pull requests, and the tools that rescue you when things go wrong.
topics.intro: Git is the first tool you learn and the one you use every day. These notes follow the roadmap's four levels: the daily loop, GitHub and remotes, branching and pull requests, then the professional commands (rebase, stash, reset, reflog) that interviews love to ask about.

modules.title: Daily basics
modules.desc: How Git stores work, the three areas, the add–commit loop, diffs, .gitignore and safe undo.

modules.title: GitHub and remotes
modules.desc: SSH keys and tokens, origin, push, pull and fetch, READMEs in Markdown, forks vs clones.

modules.title: Branches and teamwork
modules.desc: Branches and HEAD, merges, conflicts, pull requests, commit conventions and team workflows.

modules.title: Professional level
modules.desc: Rebase, stash, cherry-pick, reset vs revert, reflog, tags, releases and GitHub extras.

topics.title: Core Java
topics.lede: The language under everything else you will learn — syntax and strings, OOP done properly, exceptions and files, collections and generics, streams and modern Java, concurrency, the JVM and the everyday tools.
topics.intro: Core Java is the base for DSA, Spring Boot and every Java interview. Move quickly through module 1 if you know the basics, and slow down for OOP (module 2) and collections (module 4) — they are asked in every interview and used in every project.

modules.title: Basics and syntax
modules.desc: JDK, JRE and JVM, types and operators, control flow, methods, arrays, strings and input/output.

modules.title: Object-oriented programming
modules.desc: Classes and constructors, the four pillars, interfaces, Object methods, nested classes, enums and records.

modules.title: Exceptions and files
modules.desc: The exception hierarchy, try-with-resources, custom exceptions, best practices and java.nio.file.

modules.title: Collections and generics
modules.desc: List, Set, Map and Queue, how HashMap works inside, Comparable vs Comparator, generics and PECS.

modules.title: Modern and functional Java
modules.desc: Lambdas, method references, streams and collectors, Optional, date-time, Java 17–25 features.

modules.title: Multithreading and concurrency
modules.desc: Threads, race conditions, locks and atomics, executors, CompletableFuture, deadlocks, virtual threads.

modules.title: JVM and memory
modules.label: Interview
modules.desc: Stack vs heap, garbage collection, class loading, equals and hashCode contracts.

modules.title: Tools every Java developer uses
modules.desc: The IntelliJ debugger, Maven and Gradle, JUnit 5, JDBC with PreparedStatement, logging with SLF4J.

topics.title: SQL & Databases
topics.lede: SQL from your first SELECT to window functions, then how to design a schema, how indexes and transactions really work, and where NoSQL, Redis and migrations fit in.
topics.intro: Modules 1–3 are pure SQL — run every query yourself on PostgreSQL and predict the result first. Modules 4–6 are how databases are designed and how they work inside; they make you strong in interviews and in real Spring Boot work.

modules.title: SQL basics
modules.desc: Tables and keys, SELECT and filters, NULL logic, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE, DDL, types, constraints.

modules.title: Intermediate SQL
modules.desc: Aggregates, GROUP BY and HAVING, every join, subqueries, set operations, CASE and functions.

modules.title: Advanced SQL
modules.label: Must for interviews
modules.desc: CTEs and recursive queries, window functions, views, procedures, triggers, classic interview queries.

modules.title: Database design
modules.desc: ER diagrams, relationships, keys, normalization to BCNF, naming conventions and data types.

modules.title: How databases work inside
modules.label: Must for interviews
modules.desc: B-tree indexes, EXPLAIN, transactions and ACID, isolation levels, locking, pooling and N+1.

modules.title: Beyond relational
modules.label: Concepts
modules.desc: SQL vs NoSQL, Redis, MongoDB, CAP, replication, sharding and schema migrations.

topics.title: Spring Boot & Backend
topics.lede: Build secure, tested, production-ready REST APIs with Spring Boot — dependency injection and configuration, REST design, Spring Data JPA, Spring Security with JWT, testing, production features, and the basics of microservices and messaging.
topics.intro: Grow one project — the job-portal API (Project 2) — through these modules, adding one layer each week. Modules 1–5 are a must, module 6 makes your project look professional, and module 7 comes in month 9 alongside system design.

modules.title: Spring fundamentals
modules.desc: IoC and DI, beans, scopes and lifecycle, configuration and profiles, how auto-configuration works.

modules.title: REST APIs
modules.desc: HTTP and REST design, controllers, DTOs and mapping, validation, error handling, paging, OpenAPI.

modules.title: Data access with Spring Data JPA
modules.desc: Entities and repositories, queries, relationships, fetching and N+1, @Transactional, Flyway.

modules.title: Security
modules.desc: The filter chain, users and BCrypt, JWT login, roles, CORS and CSRF, refresh tokens, OAuth2.

modules.title: Testing
modules.desc: JUnit and Mockito, MockMvc and @DataJpaTest slices, @SpringBootTest, Testcontainers, coverage.

modules.title: Production features
modules.desc: Logging, Actuator, caching with Redis, scheduling and async, files, email, HTTP clients, rate limits.

modules.title: Microservices and messaging
modules.desc: When to split, gateways, discovery, resilience, Kafka and RabbitMQ, tracing, Docker Compose.

topics.title: Data Structures & Algorithms
topics.lede: DSA in Java, organised by pattern — complexity, arrays and hashing, two pointers and sliding windows, linked lists, stacks, trees and heaps, backtracking, graphs and dynamic programming — with reusable templates and worked problems.
topics.intro: Practise 1–1.5 hours every day and aim for about 300 well-understood problems. Each topic gives the idea, how to recognise it, a Java template and classic problems with solutions and complexity. Struggle for 20–30 minutes before reading a solution, then re-solve it after 3 days and after 2 weeks.

modules.title: Foundations
modules.desc: Big-O, the Java toolkit, maths, arrays, strings, hashing, sorting, binary search, recursion and bits.

modules.title: Core patterns
modules.desc: Two pointers, sliding window, linked lists, stacks, queues, trees, BSTs, heaps, intervals, matrices.

modules.title: Advanced
modules.desc: Backtracking, greedy, graphs and graph algorithms, dynamic programming and tries.

modules.title: Polish
modules.label: Revision
modules.desc: A revision system, the pattern cheat sheet, interview technique, contests, segment and Fenwick trees.

topics.title: Frontend
topics.lede: The frontend a backend developer needs — how the web works, semantic HTML, modern CSS layout, JavaScript done properly, React with hooks and routing, and connecting React to your Spring Boot API.
topics.intro: The goal is a clean, working UI for your own APIs, not becoming a frontend specialist. Learn JavaScript properly before React — most React confusion is really JavaScript confusion.

modules.title: How the web works
modules.desc: Requests and responses, how a page renders, and the DevTools you will live in.

modules.title: HTML
modules.desc: Structure and semantics, forms and validation, tables, accessibility, meta tags and SEO.

modules.title: CSS
modules.desc: Selectors and specificity, the box model, Flexbox, Grid, positioning, responsive design, Tailwind.

modules.title: JavaScript
modules.desc: Types and coercion, functions and closures, arrays and objects, the DOM, this, async and fetch.

modules.title: React
modules.desc: Vite, JSX and props, state and effects, forms, React Router, Context, custom hooks, TanStack Query.

modules.title: Connecting React to your Spring Boot API
modules.desc: Axios and fetch, CORS, JWT login, protected routes, backend errors, env vars and builds.

modules.title: Later, for full-stack roles
modules.desc: TypeScript, Next.js, Redux Toolkit or Zustand, and frontend testing.

topics.title: DevOps & Deployment
topics.lede: Ship your app — the Linux command line, networking for developers, Docker and Compose, CI/CD with GitHub Actions, deployment on AWS and simpler platforms, and monitoring once it is live.
topics.intro: You need a working level, not a DevOps career: enough to deploy and debug your own app. The target is simple — a push to main tests your code and puts the new version live automatically.

modules.title: Linux and the command line
modules.desc: Files, permissions, processes and ports, text tools, packages, SSH, editors and bash scripts.

modules.title: Networking for developers
modules.desc: IPs and ports, DNS, HTTPS and TLS, TCP vs UDP, firewalls and Nginx as a reverse proxy.

modules.title: Docker
modules.desc: Images and containers, Dockerfiles and multi-stage builds, volumes, networks, Compose, secrets.

modules.title: CI/CD with GitHub Actions
modules.desc: Workflows, a Maven CI job, building and pushing images, deploying, secrets, branch protection, Jenkins.

modules.title: Cloud and deployment
modules.desc: AWS EC2, RDS, S3 and IAM, a full deploy runbook, domains and HTTPS, Render, Railway and Vercel.

modules.title: Monitoring and later topics
modules.desc: Logs, health checks, uptime, Prometheus and Grafana, Kubernetes and Terraform basics.

topics.title: System Design
topics.lede: Design software at both levels — low-level design (clean code, SOLID, design patterns and classic LLD problems in Java) and high-level design (scaling, caching, databases, queues, distributed patterns and classic HLD problems).
topics.intro: Freshers are mostly asked LLD and basic HLD; deep HLD matters more after one or two years of experience. For every building block ask two questions — what problem does it solve, and what does it cost? Remember trade-offs, not memorised answers.

modules.title: Design principles
modules.desc: Cohesion and coupling, SOLID with Java, DRY, KISS and YAGNI, clean code, UML diagrams.

modules.title: Design patterns
modules.desc: Creational, structural and behavioural patterns in Java — and where Spring uses them.

modules.title: LLD interview problems
modules.desc: The LLD method, concurrency in designs, and ten classic problems designed and coded in Java.

modules.title: HLD fundamentals
modules.label: Must (concepts)
modules.desc: Communication styles, latency and throughput, estimates, scaling, availability and CAP.

modules.title: Building blocks
modules.label: Must (concepts)
modules.desc: DNS, CDNs, load balancers, gateways and rate limiting, caching, database scaling, queues, storage.

modules.title: Distributed system patterns
modules.desc: Microservices, idempotency and retries, sagas, resilience, unique IDs and observability.

modules.title: HLD interview practice
modules.desc: The 45-minute method and ten classic HLD problems worked end to end.

topics.title: CS Fundamentals
topics.lede: The four theory subjects most campus and product-company interviews ask — operating systems, computer networks, DBMS and OOP — explained simply, with worked examples and the most-asked questions.
topics.intro: Give these about four weeks in total, mostly in months 9–11, and keep one page of your own notes per subject. The classic question that ties everything together — what happens when you type a URL and press Enter — is answered step by step in module 2.

modules.title: Operating systems
modules.label: Interview
modules.desc: Processes and threads, CPU scheduling, synchronization, deadlocks, paging and virtual memory.

modules.title: Computer networks
modules.label: Interview
modules.desc: OSI and TCP/IP, IP addressing, TCP vs UDP, HTTP and HTTPS, DNS, and typing a URL.

modules.title: DBMS theory
modules.label: Interview
modules.desc: Keys, functional dependencies and normal forms, ACID, schedules, concurrency control, indexing.

modules.title: OOP theory
modules.label: Interview
modules.desc: The four pillars, abstract classes vs interfaces, overloading vs overriding, SOLID, classic questions.
